To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a joint learning framework to improve cross-domain sentiment classification; (2) we propose two auxiliary tasks that are used for inducing a sentence embedding that works well across domains; (3) we propose to use the same neural network architecture for both the sentence embedding and the sentiment classifier; (4) we show that our proposed model outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in cross-domain sentiment classification
the proposed method can be used to learn a sentence embedding that works well for cross-domain sentiment classification, and that it can outperform other methods on several benchmark datasets.

(i) joint training of the sentence embedding and the sentiment classifier outperforms the state-of-the-art methods; (ii) joint training of a sentence embedding and a sentiment classifier with auxiliary tasks outperforms the joint training with only the sentiment classification objective.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to use the auxiliary tasks to improve the generalization ability of a neural network model.
the problem of learning representations for text documents.
the following question: How to improve cross-domain sentiment classification by learning sentence embeddings?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the paper proposes a new method to improve cross-domain sentiment classification.
the proposed model outperforms the baseline model in all cases.
the joint model outperformed the other models on all datasets and that the joint model with the additional auxiliary tasks outperformed the joint model without the auxiliary tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an end-to-end joint learning model that can effectively leverage auxiliary tasks to improve cross-domain sentence embedding for sentiment classification.

we propose a new model for crossdomain sentiment classification that jointly learns a sentence embedding and a classifier with two auxiliary tasks, and the proposed model outperforms the state-of-the-art baselines on five benchmark datasets.
we propose a joint learning framework that learns a sentence embedding and a sentiment classifier together with the help of two auxiliary tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
auxiliary tasks and joint learning are effective for learning sentence embeddings that work well across domains.
it is beneficial to jointly learn the sentence embedding and the sentiment classifier for cross-domain sentiment classification.
joint learning of a sentence embedding together with a downstream sentiment classifier can be very helpful in cross-domain sentiment classification.
